nodes.label: Frame 07101 - Infrared Night Capture, Sparse Flock (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-24 22:06:12)
nodes.description: Monochrome infrared night-vision still - the camera has switched to IR cut-filter-removed mode, so the image is greyscale with washed-out low-saturation tones and the red feeder cones appear as neutral grey. Bird density is the lowest of the six frames; small birds are loosely scattered with visible bare litter between them. Strong barrel/fisheye curvature is evident in the bowed feed line and the arcing dark cable near the bottom edge.
nodes.rationale: Represents the hardest imaging regime in the dataset - low contrast, no colour channel information, and IR glare on the plastic feeders - so bird/litter separation must rely on shape and texture alone.

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Mode Capture Regime
nodes.description: The automatic camera mode in which the IR cut filter is withdrawn under low light, yielding monochrome frames with compressed dynamic range, IR hotspots on plastic surfaces, and no usable colour channel. Two of the six frames in this chunk are in this mode.
nodes.rationale: It splits the corpus into two visually incompatible domains from a single physical camera, meaning colour-dependent cues such as the red feeder cones vanish entirely and any model must either be colour-invariant or be trained on both domains.

nodes.label: Frame Index Does Not Track Chronology
nodes.description: Filename sequence numbers are not monotonic in acquisition time: frame07101 is stamped 2022-02-24 22:06 while the lower-numbered frame06701 is stamped 2022-03-01 23:05, a six-day inversion. Numbering therefore reflects extraction or concatenation order across multiple source recordings, not a single continuous timeline.
nodes.rationale: Any temporal split, tracking pass, or 'hold out the last N frames' strategy that assumes filename order equals time order will silently interleave recording sessions; the burned-in OSD timestamp, not the index, must be treated as the authoritative time key.
